Well, this sounds that life is going to change on your side. I always admired your way of life and thought you are just upgrading to a bigger ship when “Strange Waves” was sold (of course I was only guessing).

I’m pretty sure however that both of you have so many interests and affairs of heart that I myself just look forward how life will develop on your side. I wish you the best for it …

Cheers
Jo

comments.author: 100330886@N04
comments.text:
[https://www.flickr.com/photos/italobikes-v2jo] I had an idea years ago while working in an office that it would be nice to collect sounds and pictures from places that would be nice background to think about while writing software.  I didn't take all of these pics thinking about that, but it will be nice to have these pics to contemplate in extremely different circumstances.  Especially trips like hitchhiking across Canada.  It seemed unreal at the time and even more so now.

We're glad you're along for the adventure.  Your pics of motorcycles, bicycles and mountains has us inspired to see Germany some day!

comments.author: 100330886@N04
comments.text:
[https://www.flickr.com/photos/26941526@N00] So, when I found the book on the St. Lawrence River on the shelf in the Providence Athenaeum, Steph had recognized the picture of Le Chien D'or related to some stories about Quebec City.  I thought we had stumbled on a fun mystery, but as it turns out, it is a famous tourist destination and had a famous book written about it in the late 1800's.  :)  It was fun to find and read about it.  It turns out that it is likely based on a monument in France related to a law suit around one man killing another man's dog.  

Here is the best telling of the whole situation that I could find:
www.ameriquefrancaise.org/en/article-590/The_Golden_Dog.html

Here is the Canadian reissue of the famous book:
www.mqup.ca/chien-d-or-the-golden-dog--critical-edition-l...
